dos.text: Set disablekeynav deliberately and only when you intend to lose all built-in keyboard navigation, it's checked once in the popupshowing handler, and when set, the keydown/mousemove listeners that drive arrow-key/Tab/Home/End navigation are never attached for that panel's entire lifetime, with no fallback.

donts.text: Don't call showSubView or goBack before the panel has ever been opened, openViews is only initialized inside connect(), so calling either beforehand throws a raw TypeError instead of the intended "Cannot show a subview in a closed panel" console error.

Don't assume a second showSubView/goBack call fired mid-transition queues up, both check "if (!prevPanelView.active) return" with no error or logging, so a call arriving while a transition is already in flight is just silently dropped.

behavior.text: showSubView's own JSDoc says it plainly: the public method "returns synchronously, but may eventually log an error if showing the subview fails". It calls a private async #showSubView and discards the returned promise via .catch(console.error), so a caller gets no return value to await and no thrown error, a failed transition surfaces only as a console.error sometime later (confirmed in PanelMultiView.sys.mjs at commit d8b0cd3f8ed35b6c7094e274d180ed3ef5e7e637).
